name: OPA627 / OPA637 (Burr-Brown Difet precision JFET single; OPA637 decompensated, G>=5)
tagline: Burr-Brown's Difet JFET single, long called the 'king' of op-amp rolling and prized for detail and a smooth sound, with pA bias and 4.5 nV/rtHz noise.
technology: JFET-input single op-amp. The Burr-Brown datasheet describes a high-speed, dielectrically isolated complementary NPN/PNP process with laser-trimmed Difet input circuitry. The OPA627 is unity-gain stable. The OPA637 is decompensated and stable at gains of 5 or more. TI's current SBOS165C (Jan 2025) retitles the family 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET Operational Amplifiers', and its revision history records that the Difet references were deleted.
manufacturers: Rochester Electronics (reported aftermarket for discontinued packages; not verified)

part_numbers.status: active (TI E2E 1386960, 2024: still active but 'will not be packaged for now', future production uncertain; TI suggested the OPA828ID as a pin-to-pin replacement)
part_numbers.notes: SOIC-8, A grade. Soomal reports HiFiMAN's IEM card uses 2x OPA627AU + BUF634AU. Heavily counterfeited.

New SOIC B grade that did not exist in the Burr-Brown era. It was added as a preview device before Rev C (Rev B, Apr 2024, by inference) and moved to production in SBOS165C. TI has an orderable page for it.
DIP-8, A grade. Soomal says the HiFiMAN Minibox card used a DIP OPA627 with a BUF634. New stock is aftermarket, or an AU on an adapter.

part_numbers.status: obsolete (the through-hole version is reported discontinued; no BP-specific notice seen)
part_numbers.notes: DIP-8, B grade (tighter offset and drift). A common remarking target.

part_numbers.status: unclear. In 2024, TI E2E 1386960 said TO-can stock was expected 'shortly' (about 2 months). The NRND claim is unconfirmed.
part_numbers.notes: TO-99 metal can. The current datasheet documents offset trim for TO-99 only. A DigiKey Marketplace listing from Rochester is unverified.
TO-99, military temperature grade. Appears in Burr-Brown model lists. Soomal calls SM parts 'very rare'.
Bare-die version. A datasheet titled 'OPA627-DIE Precision High-Speed DIFET Operational ...' is hosted by DigiKey. The orderable die part number and doc number were not captured.

part_numbers.status: active (OPA637 product folder ACTIVE; orderable page exists)
part_numbers.notes: SOIC-8, decompensated (G>=5). Appears in the Burr-Brown-era model list. Covered by SBOS165.
Only the discovery notes mention it. The Rev C change note mentions only the OPA627BU.
TO-99, B grade. Soomal: genuine Taiwan/US cans cost ¥250 or more, and the HiFiMAN 'gold Minibox' card uses 2 of them. By 2021 Soomal said they came only from second-hand pulled stock.

lineage.notes: Difet successor to the OPA111. PSpice macromodels dated October 1990 prove the part existed by then. The oldest datasheet edition found reads 'Printed in U.S.A. March, 1998' (confirmed).

The datasheet became SBOS165 in 2000. Rev A reads 'SEPTEMBER 2000-REVISED OCTOBER 2015'. Rev B is dated April 2024. Rev C reads 'AUGUST 2000 - REVISED JANUARY 2025'. TI names the OPA828 as its suggested alternate. PSpice literature numbers are SBOM099/SBOC118 (OPA627) and SBOM101/SBOC119 (OPA637).
Reported to sell OPA627AM/DIP stock via DigiKey Marketplace. Not verified.

key_specs.condition: f = 10 kHz (front-page figure). The 1 kHz value was not captured.
OPA637 at G = 10 (confirmed). The OPA627 16 MHz is corroborated only by a third-party EDA library.

key_specs.value: 7.5 mA max per amplifier (about 7-7.5 mA observed)
key_specs.condition: Not confirmed via web. Taken from a third-party supply budget and community fake-check guides.
The OPA627 is unity-gain stable. The OPA637 is stable at G>=5.

reputation.summary: Widely treated as the benchmark audiophile JFET single that later JFET parts are compared against. It is called the 'king' on English-language forums and 'legendary' in Japanese reviews. Soomal (China) groups the OPA627/637 with Burr-Brown's DiFET parts as warm-leaning, with full mids, strong dynamics and a spacious sound, and says they resolve HF better than the OPA111/OPA2107. Soomal also rates the OPA637 slightly above the OPA627. Critics such as Leckerton note that in blind listening it does not clearly beat cheaper parts like the AD8610. None of these characterizations were re-verified in this pass.
sonic_descriptors: warm, easy to listen to (Soomal AE-9 swap, 2020)
typical_uses: DAC post-filter / I/V stages (HiFiMAN HM-901 uses an OPA627 with an OPA2107 in the LPF, per Soomal)
Headphone amp cards: HiFiMAN IEM, balanced and Minibox cards pair it with the BUF634, per Soomal
op-amp rolling in sound cards and DACs via single-to-dual adapters
transimpedance / photodiode and instrumentation front ends
caveats: It is a single op-amp only, so dual sockets need an adapter board.
The OPA637 is unstable below a noise gain of about 5. Do not drop it into unity-gain buffer sockets.
Quiescent current is up to about 7.5 mA per amp, which means heat and battery drain.
It is one of the most counterfeited audiophile op-amps.
The DIP versions are obsolete, and in 2024 TI said the SOIC AU might not be packaged for a while (E2E 1386960).
The current TI datasheet shows pins 1/5 as NC on the molded packages, and offset trim applies to the TO-99 only.
Soomal folklore that country of origin matters (US > Taiwan > SE Asia) is not backed by any measurements.
A/B-grade differences are reportedly inaudible, and blind tests reportedly show no clear win over the AD8610. Neither claim was re-verified.

revision_history.date: September 2000 (Rev A header); Rev C header says August 2000
revision_history.changes: TI literature number assigned after the acquisition, presumably with Burr-Brown content. Served c.2004 at focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf.

Converted to TI's current format, with ESD Ratings and Product Folder blocks. Still titled 'Precision High-Speed Difet', with pins 1/5 shown as Trim. TI PSpice models still cited Rev A in June 2022. The detailed change list was not captured.

The date is confirmed by the Rev C history ('Changes from Revision B (April 2024)'). Per the revision history, the Difet references were deleted and the OPA627BU preview device was added (attributed to Rev B by inference). The part was retitled 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET'. The molded-package pins 1/5 became NC, with trim for TO-99 only, in Rev B or C.
The OPA627BU changed from preview to production data. The first-issue date in the header now reads August 2000.

A TI E2E thread (e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/1393043/opa627-opa627au) says the OPA627 was introduced in 1989 in plastic DIP and metal can (TO-99) only. The 1990 Burr-Brown IC Data Book Supplement 33b (bitsavers) reportedly includes the OPA627. The PDS base number is inferred from the later PDS-998H.
The SOIC package (the AU/BU parts) was added in the mid-1990s and appears in the 1995 Burr-Brown IC Data Book (per the TI E2E thread). No standalone datasheet copy with this letter was found.

Search summaries identify PDS-998H as the Burr-Brown document number of the 'OPA627/637 Precision High-Speed Difet Operational Amplifiers' sheet printed in March 1998 (the Carnegie copy). It covers plastic DIP, SOIC and TO-99. The letter H implies at least seven earlier editions (A-G), none of which were located.

silicon_changes.when: SBOS165B (April 2024) / SBOS165C (January 2025, OPA627BU moved from preview to production); after June 2022, when TI models still cited Rev A
silicon_changes.identification: New documentation is SBOS165B/C, titled 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET Operational Amplifiers'. In the current pin table, molded-package pins 1/5 are NC, and external offset trim is documented for TO-99 only. The OPA627BU orderable exists only from 2024-2025. No PCN or date-code cut-over was found; BB-logo and pre-2024 TI parts keep functional trim pins.
silicon_changes.summary: TI's 2024-2025 rewrite deleted all 'Difet' references, added a B-grade SOIC (OPA627BU), and turned the molded packages' offset-trim pins into NC. For the sister OPA132, TI E2E 1517005 attributes the same change to a 'new FAB change and design'; the diyAudio thread says trim is no longer functional from Rev C because the parts are made with higher precision (one poster speculates the pads are simply no longer bonded). This points to a new die or process under the same part numbers, but TI has not confirmed a silicon change for the OPA627 specifically and no PCN was found.

spec_deltas.after: NC; trim documented for TO-99 only (SBOS165B/C)
AU and BU (BU production data in Rev C, Jan 2025)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. No before/after measurements were found. Circuits that null offset through pins 1/5 lose that adjustment on new molded parts. Impressions formed on Burr-Brown-era parts may not carry over.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - offset-trim circuits do not work on new molded parts, and the electrical spec deltas between Rev A and Rev C were not captured
silicon_changes.verification: WebSearch confirmed the Rev B (Apr 2024) to Rev C (Jan 2025) history, the deleted Difet references, BU going to production, and (via diyAudio) molded pins 1/5 now NC with trim only on TO-99. The die change itself remains inferred from the OPA132 sister part.

silicon_changes.when: 2024 (TI E2E thread 1386960, 'Is the OPA627AU end of life?')
silicon_changes.identification: Status stayed Active, but TI said the SOIC-8 AU was temporarily not being packaged, and BU / TO-can stock was expected in about 2 months.
silicon_changes.summary: Temporary supply suspension of the OPA627AU while the family moved to the 2024-2025 documentation (and likely silicon) described above. TI named OPA828ID as the recommended pin-to-pin replacement for the AU. The OPA828 is a different SiGe JFET-input die, not the same silicon.

spec_deltas.after: Active, SOIC-8 temporarily not packaged (2024); OPA828ID suggested as replacement

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None to the silicon. Buyers steered to the OPA828ID get a different die with different noise, bandwidth and bias characteristics.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - the AU supply was interrupted, and TI's suggested replacement is a different die
silicon_changes.verification: Split out of the Rev B/C entry. WebSearch confirmed that the E2E thread says the AU is active but temporarily not packaged, with OPA828ID as the pin-to-pin replacement and BU/TO-can stock expected in about 2 months.

silicon_changes.when: after 2000 (TI acquisition); exact transfer date unknown
silicon_changes.identification: Collector folklore: a Burr-Brown logo, a pre-2000 date code, and US or Taiwan origin.
silicon_changes.summary: Soomal (2016) ranks Taiwan-made parts second only to US-made, and ahead of SE-Asian-made. Japanese sellers claim Burr-Brown-era parts use a different process rule and thicker bond wires. No vendor document, PCN or measurement supports this.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - same pinout and specs; the practical risk is that 'vintage BB' listings attract remarked fakes
silicon_changes.verification: Not searched (folklore kind, outside the verification priority); kept as folklore-unconfirmed with no documentary support.

counterfeit_notes: One of the most counterfeited audiophile op-amps. In 2014, ZeptoBars decapped a $2.7 'OPA627' from China/eBay and found an Analog Devices AD744 die (marked 'AD'/'B744'). The genuine die shows at least 4 laser-trimmed resistors and the fake shows 1; the AD744 has about 3x the noise and 0.5 mV offset against 0.1 mV. OPA602 and AD711-class donor dies are also reported but were not verified. Community checks (Head-Fi, diyAudio, not re-verified) are quiescent current of about 7-7.5 mA plus square-wave and slew tests. The pin 1-5 trim-resistance check is unreliable on new TI molded parts, whose pins 1/5 are NC. Maimai-audio (a single blog) lists OPA627AU lot codes A3L, AEB, AKG, D5L, K4D, LAE, LDE, LPS, MDE and T3K as almost all fake. Soomal makes several points: TO-99 OPA637BM selling for tens of yuan are fake; every 'custom metal-can' version is fake; some fakes put an ordinary PDIP chip inside a metal shell; and SM parts are very rare. The DIP versions are obsolete, so any 'new' OPA627AP/BP is suspect. Buy the SOIC AU/BU from TI or an authorized distributor.
alternatives: OPA828 / OPA2828 (TI's suggested alternate for the OPA627. TI E2E 1386960 names the OPA828ID as a pin-to-pin replacement for the OPA627AU. TI describes it as 'the next generation OPA627 and OPA827'.)
ADA4627-1 / ADA4637-1 (ADI JFET; the ADA4637 is the decompensated analogue of the OPA637)

Is there a TI PCN or E2E statement confirming a new OPA627/637 die or trim process in 2024? None was found.
Current status of the TO-99 AM/BM/SM and OPA637 TO-99 parts. TI E2E (2024) said TO-can stock was coming, so the NRND claim is unconfirmed.
Does an OPA637BU exist? What is the orderable part number and doc number for the OPA627-DIE?

refuted_claims: The discovery hint that the TO-99 AM/BM/SM are out of production per TI E2E 2024 is contradicted. In 2024, TI E2E 1386960 said 'OPA627BU or TO-CAN package will be in stock shortly'. TO-99 status was changed to unclear.
'Revision A (April 2015)' is refuted. SBOS165A reads 'SEPTEMBER 2000-REVISED OCTOBER 2015'.
'Metal-can fakes put a DIP die inside the can' misstates Soomal, who says some fakes put an ordinary PDIP chip inside a metal shell.
corrections: SBOS165C is confirmed as current, with the header 'AUGUST 2000 - REVISED JANUARY 2025'. Rev B is dated April 2024, and the OPA627BU moved from preview to production in Rev C. The symlink entry was raised to high confidence.
The Difet references deleted, the OPA627BU preview added and the 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET' title are confirmed. The deletion and the BU preview are attributed to Rev B by inference.

Molded-package pins 1/5 as NC with trim for TO-99 only is confirmed via diyAudio 418419. TI's OPA132 E2E explanation (higher-precision manufacturing) was added. The silicon_changes confidence was raised to medium for the documentation change only; the die change remains unconfirmed.
OPA627AU status refined from TI E2E 1386960: still active but temporarily not packaged, with the OPA828ID as the suggested pin-to-pin replacement. OPA627AP is confirmed obsolete.
The OPA637 80 MHz GBW (G=10) and 135 V/us are confirmed. The OPA637 product folder is ACTIVE.

New datasheet copies added: ti.com symlink opa637.pdf; the SBOS165A diagram page; the TI.com.cn viewer; Burr-Brown-edition copies at audiophonics.fr, hifituning24.de, studylib and datasheetcatalog; the octopart OPA627BP copy; radiolocman OPA637; ciiva; and an OPA627-DIE datasheet on DigiKey. OPA627-DIE was added as a part number.
The Mouser, Cimarron and b-cdn copies were identified as freezing Rev A (Oct 2015), and the Carnegie copy as the Burr-Brown March 1998 edition.
The pin 1-5 trim-resistance fake check is flagged as invalid on new TI molded parts.
claims_confirmed: SBOS165C is current, with the header 'AUGUST 2000 - REVISED JANUARY 2025'. The Rev C history records the OPA627BU changing from preview to production and gives the Rev B date as April 2024 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).
The current title is 'OPA6x7 Precision, High-Speed JFET Operational Amplifiers' (https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/OPA627 ; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa637.pdf).
The revision history records that the Difet references were deleted and the OPA627BU preview device was added (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).
SBOS165A reads 'SEPTEMBER 2000-REVISED OCTOBER 2015' and includes ESD ratings of HBM +/-2500 V and CDM +/-1000 V for SOIC (https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/405/opa627-406898.pdf).

The Rev A copy shows 'Trim 5 Trim 1' and 'Product Folder / Sample & Buy' (https://www.cimarrontechnology.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/opa627.pdf ; https://datasheets.b-cdn.net/files/OPA627AU-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-60566259.pdf).

Molded-package trim pins are now NC and offset adjustment applies to TO-99 only (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/opa132-opa627-and-other-ti-bb-op-amps-no-longer-have-an-offset-trim-terminal.418419/).

TI attributes the NC trim pins on the OPA132 (from Rev C) to higher-precision manufacturing (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1517005/opa132-changed-opa132-pin-1-and-pin-8-from-offset-trim-to-nc).

In 2024, TI said the OPA627AU was still active but 'will not be packaged for now', named the OPA828ID as a pin-to-pin replacement, and said BU/TO-can stock would come shortly (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/1386960/opa627-is-the-opa627au-end-of-life).
OPA637: 80 MHz GBW at G=10, 135 V/us slew, product ACTIVE (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA637).
The OPA627BU and OPA637AU orderable pages exist (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA627/part-details/OPA627BU ; https://www.ti.com/product/OPA637/part-details/OPA637AU).
OPA627: 4.5 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz, 55 V/us, 100 uV max Vos, 0.8 uV/C, 5 pA max IB, +/-4.5 to +/-18 V (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf).

The Burr-Brown edition is 'Printed in U.S.A. March, 1998' and describes a dielectrically isolated complementary NPN/PNP process with laser-trimmed Difet input (https://instrumentation.obs.carnegiescience.edu/ccd/parts/OPA627.pdf ; https://www.audiophonics.fr/images2/8434/opa627.pdf).
No OPA627-specific PCN was found in TI/Mouser PCN search results (https://www.ti.com/quality-reliability/quality/product-change-notification.html).

revision_chain_notes:
Burr-Brown OPA627/OPA637 combined sheet, document PDS-998. The base number was newly identified, and letters A-G are still missing:
- original, 1989 (introduced in PDIP and TO-99). The 1990 IC Data Book Supplement 33b (bitsavers) reportedly contains it.
- a mid-1990s edition that added SOIC (in the 1995 Linear Products Data Book).
- PDS-998H, March 1998 (the Carnegie copy). Two search summaries give PDS-998H for this edition.
Missing: every earlier letter (PDS-998 through PDS-998G) as a standalone sheet, with dates. Databook copies (bitsavers 1990 Supplement 33b, rsp-italy 1995 Linear Products, archive.org 1998 Linear/Mixed Signal) are the best leads for the pre-1998 editions.

TI SBOS165:
- original, Aug/Sep 2000. No copy was confirmed. Candidates are the alldatasheet TI 16-page copies (170755 OPA627BM, 170761 OPA637BM), the older radiolocman uploads (di=82271, 82272) and focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa627.pdf (Wayback).
- Rev A, Oct 2015. Known. alldatasheet 783815 (37 pages) is probably Rev A, but this is not shown.
- Rev B, Apr 2024. Still no copy found; a search for SBOS165B returned only Rev A and Burr-Brown copies.
- Rev C, Jan 2025. Current.
- alldatasheet 516678 (23 pages) is an unidentified TI edition.

OPA637: no separate OPA637-only sheet was found in either the Burr-Brown or the TI era. All OPA637 copies (alldatasheet 56796-56801 including the OPA637SM, datasheetcatalog, alldatasheet TI 170761) appear to be the combined OPA627/OPA637 document.
